title: Durable verification receipt dispatch
description: Objective: compose the real verification process wrapper and evidence pipeline into the durable Foundation attempt path. Deliverable: a daemon service and focused tests that read the exact stored input/result/runtime identities from Durable Claude attempt dispatch, activate one verification effect, execute the sealed recipe, persist the immutable EvidenceReceipt and its stdout/stderr/exit bindings, and expose a read model for later review/closure. NOT in scope: review decisions, goal closure, provider launch, or E2E fixtures. Depends on the Verification process wrapper and Durable Claude attempt dispatch tasks. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/evidence/foundation-verification-contracts.ts/.js, foundation-verification-service.ts/.js, and foundation-verification-service.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The service loads the exact durable input manifest, result manifest, runtime observation, and sealed recipe by identity; caller-supplied replacements or stale hashes refuse with stable code/layer before execution.

One atomic verification activation precedes the shell-free process wrapper, and a green observed run produces one immutable EvidenceReceipt binding recipe, input/result trees, runtime, stdout/stderr, exit, and timing digests.
FAILED remains a proven failed receipt while UNKNOWN, truncated, mismatched, or unverified execution cannot create an authoritative passing receipt; each refusal asserts exact reason and layer.
Replay leaves exactly one verification run and one receipt row; a conflict or changed candidate produces a distinct refusal and no overwritten history.
The production read model returns prior receipts byte-identically for review/closure, all runner/daemon/repo gates exit 0, and production files stay below 250 lines.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
CONTRACTS FIRST — create `apps/daemon/src/evidence/foundation-verification-contracts.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./foundation-verification-contracts.ts";`, LF ending; apps/daemon requires a physical bridge per production module and the guard byte-compares).
It declares this service's own frozen reason-code and layer vocabularies — `Object.freeze([...] as const)` plus derived union types, the shape every contract in this repo uses, so a test can ITERATE them at runtime. Scope them to what THIS service can refuse: an identity that does not resolve, a stale or replaced hash, an activation that could not be committed, a candidate that changed between load and execution, a replay conflict. Do NOT restate the wrapper's own codes — `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES` and `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS` already cover execution failures and travel through unchanged. Two vocabularies for one condition is the defect that got a sibling task rejected.
EVERY DECLARED CODE MUST HAVE A PRODUCER. A code no layer can emit cannot fail closed; task-6cbff010 was rejected in round 2 for exactly three such orphans. Before the gate, grep each member and confirm a production emit site plus a code+layer test — or drop it.
Also declare the service's input and result types. The input names identities, never payloads: the durable attempt's identity, the sealed recipe's identity, and the verification's own correlation. Anything the caller could supply as a REPLACEMENT for durable state must be structurally absent from the input type — that is DoD 1's "caller-supplied replacements refuse", enforced by making them unrepresentable rather than validated away.
Keep under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts).

VOCABULARIES. FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_CODES holds 12 frozen members, FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_LAYERS 5, both `Object.freeze([...] as const)` with derived union types so a test can ITERATE them at runtime. Codes: REQUEST_MALFORMED, ATTEMPT_UNPROVEN, RECIPE_UNRESOLVED, RECIPE_SEAL_INVALID, CANDIDATE_STALE, ACTIVATION_UNCOMMITTED, CANDIDATE_CHANGED, REPLAY_CONFLICT, CAPTURE_TRUNCATED, EXECUTION_UNVERIFIED, RECEIPT_AMBIGUOUS, RECEIPT_UNREADABLE. Layers: DAEMON_VERIFICATION_{REQUEST,IDENTITY,ACTIVATION,EXECUTION,RECEIPT}. I am carrying all 12 as a debt to discharge at step 7: the plan's rule is that a code no layer can emit cannot fail closed, so each gets a production emit site plus a code+layer test, or it gets dropped from the frozen list before the gate. The two that most need watching are CANDIDATE_STALE and CANDIDATE_CHANGED, which look like one condition and are not: STALE is the caller's expectedRecordDigest disagreeing with the durable record at LOAD, CHANGED is the durable record moving BETWEEN load and execution. Different producers, different times, and step 4's mismatched-candidate case pins the second. If step 5 cannot produce both distinctly, the weaker one gets dropped rather than left orphaned.

NO RESTATEMENT OF THE WRAPPER'S CODES, which is the defect that got the sibling task rejected. There is deliberately no daemon code for a failed spawn, a timeout, an output overflow or a receipt-binding fault: VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES and RUNNER_EVIDENCE_ERROR_CODES already name those. Pass-through is structural, not conventional — FoundationVerificationRefused is a union discriminated by a `source` field over FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_REFUSAL_SOURCES (DAEMON_VERIFICATION, FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT, VERIFIER_PROCESS, RUNNER_SUPERVISOR, RUNNER_EVIDENCE), and each arm is typed to ITS OWN authority's code and layer unions. `carryWrapperRefusal` is total over the wrapper's three-way refusal union and re-codes nothing; `carryAttemptRefusal` copies the store's code and reads its layer from `refusedBy`, which is how that record spells it. A restamp is now a type error rather than a review catch.

DoD 1 ENFORCED BY THE TYPE, NOT BY A VALIDATOR. FoundationVerificationRequest carries exactly five fields — attemptAggregateId, candidateRoot, expectedRecordDigest, recipeAggregateId, verificationId. There is NO field for an input manifest, result manifest, runtime observation, recipe body or receipt, so a caller-supplied replacement for durable state is unrepresentable rather than validated away, and a later refactor cannot quietly stop calling the check. expectedRecordDigest is the caller's belief about WHICH record it is verifying, never a substitute for the record.

DESIGN DECISION THAT THE PLAN DID NOT SETTLE, disclosed rather than assumed. DoD 1 requires the sealed recipe to be loaded BY IDENTITY, but I measured that no durable recipe store exists anywhere: `buildVerificationRecipe`/`VerificationRecipe` have zero non-test references in apps/daemon/src and packages/store/src, the durable attempt record body carries no recipe field (attemptRecordBody spells inputManifest, resultManifest, observation, registration, the identity set and the stdout/stderr digests, and nothing else), and the two daemon files matching /recipe/ are the orchestrator's older NodeMission-based verifier runner, an unrelated lane. So "load the recipe by identity" has nothing to load from unless this task also makes a recipe durable. I therefore declared FoundationRecipeRegistration: declaring a recipe is how one is CREATED, and from the sealed event onward it is loaded by identity and never again accepted from a caller. This keeps DoD 1 honest instead of quietly letting the caller pass a recipe body on the verify path. If the epic intends recipe sealing to belong to a different task, this is the seam to move and I want it flagged now rather than at QA.

CONSUMED RATHER THAN REIMPLEMENTED: the canonical-bytes primitives (encodeFoundationPayload/decodeFoundationPayload/sha256Hex/sameBytes/isRecord/textOf/exactKeys) already exist in work/foundation-attempt-codec.ts and will be imported by the service at step 5, not rewritten — a second canonical form would be a second definition of the bytes review and closure hash. That file belongs to task-6cbff010 and stays untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 1 — identity loading and the refusals that must happen BEFORE any process starts. Create `foundation-verification-service.test.ts` against the not-yet-existing service, driving a REAL SqliteEventStore opened per test and closed in a `finally` on every exit path (a held handle kills the vitest worker).
DoD 1 CASES, each asserting the exact code AND layer: the durable input manifest, result manifest, runtime observation and sealed recipe are loaded BY IDENTITY through the landed readers (`readStoredFoundationAttempt`, `readFoundationAttemptRecord`, `readDurableFoundationObservation`); an identity that resolves to nothing refuses; a hash that no longer matches the durable record refuses; a recipe whose seal fails `recipeSealMatches` refuses.
THE ORDERING ASSERTION IS THE POINT OF THIS STEP: every one of those refusals must occur BEFORE the process wrapper is invoked. Assert it observably — drive with a launcher that records invocations and assert ZERO invocations on every refusal path, the same shape task-6cbff010's `forgedCalls 0` assertion used. A refusal that happens after a process already ran is not a refusal, it is a cleanup.
AND ASSERT THE ATOMIC ACTIVATION ORDERING from DoD 2: the verification activation is committed BEFORE the wrapper runs. Read the durable state back and assert that, for a refusal after activation, an activation exists with no run — never a run with no activation. That direction matters: a run without a committed activation is an effect nothing authorised.
Every fixture valid at the earlier layers so the intended refusal answers — the store, the dispatch readers, the recipe seal and this service can each refuse, and a code-only assertion detaches the moment a different one answers first.

(1) The broken-seal case first called a `corruptSealForTest` hook on the service — test-owned authority, banned by task rail 2. (2) The not-PROVEN case originally ran against a PROVEN fixture and asserted `expect(outcome.ok).not.toBe(undefined)` — a tautology that passes forever. Replaced with a real `unprovenGround`, which drives the SAME production writer `recordProvenFoundationAttempt` with a capture answer missing its required keys so the writer takes its own advisory branch and persists truthClass UNKNOWN; the case asserts the durable record really reads UNKNOWN before asserting the refusal, so it cannot be answered by a different layer.

FIXTURES ARE PRODUCTION-CHAIN ONLY. Nothing hand-forges an activation: the ground runs the real activation ingress, then the real `createFoundationLauncherAuthority` GRANT_CONSUMED -> PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED -> PROCESS_OBSERVED tail, then the real `readDurableFoundationObservation`, then the real `recordProvenFoundationAttempt`; the input manifest comes from the runner's `buildInputManifest` and the scope observation from `observeScope`, never hand-written. The record digest is always read back through `readFoundationAttemptRecord` rather than taken from the writer's return value — the UNKNOWN ground's writer answers with a refusal and carries no digest.

ONE HAZARD FOUND WHILE WRITING, worth the next reader's attention: `runVerifierProcess` keeps a MODULE-LEVEL run registry keyed by grantId, so two cases sharing an effect intent would share a grant and the second would silently ADOPT the first one's run instead of starting its own. Every case therefore derives its own intent, aggregate and grant from its label. This will matter again in step 6's replay cases, where adoption is the behaviour under test rather than an accident.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, PART 2 — FAILED versus UNKNOWN, which is this task's hardest distinction and DoD 3's whole content. A PROVEN FAILED verification is authoritative evidence: the recipe ran, the verifier answered, and the answer was no. An UNVERIFIED run is not evidence of anything. Collapsing them either way is the defect — treating UNKNOWN as failure invents a verdict, and treating FAILED as UNKNOWN discards one.
Drive through the real `runVerifierProcess` and pin, each with exact code and layer:
- GREEN OBSERVED RUN → exactly one immutable `EvidenceReceipt` built by `buildEvidenceReceipt`, binding recipe, input and result trees, runtime, stdout, stderr, exit and timing digests. Assert the receipt's digest recomputes via `receiptDigestInput`, and assert it came from the runner's builder rather than a locally-composed lookalike.
- FAILED OBSERVED RUN → a receipt that is PROVEN and FAILED. Assert it is durable and authoritative, not refused.
- TRUNCATED capture (`MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES`) → cannot produce an authoritative PASSING receipt, and the truncation is RECORDED rather than silently dropped. A truncated capture whose recorded output happens to look green is exactly how a false pass gets minted.
- TIMED-OUT run (`MAX_VERIFIER_RUN_MS`, with `VERIFIER_REAP_GRACE_MS` for the reap) → refuses; assert the run terminates rather than hanging, and bound the test itself.
- MISMATCHED candidate — the input or result tree changed between load and execution → refuses with a distinct code, no receipt.
- UNVERIFIED execution → no authoritative passing receipt under any circumstance. Assert this as a PROPERTY over the whole non-green set rather than per case, so a case added later cannot escape it.
USE `hermeticVerifierEnvironment` for the process environment rather than assembling one — the wrapper publishes it precisely so a caller cannot widen the environment a verifier sees, and a locally-built env would be a second, drifting definition of hermetic.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED PART 2 LANDED. Test file now 830 lines; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` still reports exactly ONE error, the expected TS2307 for the not-yet-written service. Nothing green is being claimed.

SIX CASES ADDED, all driving REAL child processes through the REAL `createNodeProcessLauncher` and the REAL `runVerifierProcess`. The recording launcher from step 3 is used only to prove ABSENCE; every case that ACCEPTS evidence spawns an actual process, because a receipt minted from a stand-in would prove only that the stand-in was believed. argv fixtures are real node invocations: exit 0 (green), exit 3 (failed), a 2MiB stdout flood (truncation, against MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES = 1MiB), and a setInterval hang (timeout).

GREEN: asserts exactly ONE RECEIPTED event counted from durable state rather than from the return value, verdict PASSED, authority PROVEN_RECEIPT, the receipt bound to the durable inputManifest and resultManifest sha256s read back out of the attempt record, and the stdout/stderr/exit bindings the receipt itself does not carry.
FAILED: asserts a failed run stays PROVEN, authoritative and durable — ok:true, verdict FAILED, exitCode 3, ONE receipt row, and readable back through the read model. This is the direction that most often gets collapsed: the recipe ran, the verifier answered, and the answer was no. That is evidence, not an absence of it.
TRUNCATED: asserts the wrapper's own VERIFIER_PROCESS_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW / CAPTURE travels through unrestamped, NO receipt is written, and the truncation is RECORDED on a durable UNKNOWN row (stdoutTruncated true, truthClass UNKNOWN) rather than silently dropped.
TIMED OUT: asserts VERIFIER_PROCESS_TIMED_OUT / CAPTURE, no receipt, and that the run actually TERMINATED — wall-clock bounded under 20s with the case itself capped at 30s, so a hang fails instead of masquerading as a slow suite.
CANDIDATE CHANGED: a genuine concurrent writer, not a hook. A launcher wrapping the real one commits a SECOND durable RECORDED event through the store's own port at the exact moment the child starts; the service's post-run re-read then refuses and mints no receipt.
THE PROPERTY: asserted over the whole non-green set in one loop (flood, hang, exit 9) with a positive scenario count asserted first so it cannot pass vacuously — for every non-green run, the outcome is either a refusal or a PROVEN FAILED verdict, never PASSED; the read model never returns PASSED; and at most one RECEIPTED event exists.

THREE DECLARED CODES DROPPED AS ORPHANS, measured rather than assumed — this is the defect that got task-6cbff010 rejected in round 2, so I went looking for it before the gate instead of after. (1) FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_CAPTURE_TRUNCATED: `runVerifierProcess` interrupts and refuses the moment a stream passes its bound (verifier-process-run.ts:107-111), so a truncated capture can never reach this service as a success and no daemon layer could ever emit the code. (2) FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_EXECUTION_UNVERIFIED: the wrapper only ever answers ok with `disposition: exit.exitCode === 0 ? "COMPLETED" : "FAILED"` (verifier-process-run.ts:194) — UNKNOWN and CANCELLED are refusals, never executions. (3) FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_CANDIDATE_CHANGED: a durable attempt record is IMMUTABLE, one RECORDED event, and a second makes `readStoredFoundationAttempt` refuse FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS under the STORE's code — so the daemon code would have no reachable producer. In all three cases the DoD is still met, by carrying the producer's own refusal, recording truncation on the UNKNOWN row, and asserting no-authoritative-pass as a property. The frozen list is down from 12 to 9, and every survivor has a producer I am committed to writing in step 5.

ONE ASSERTION WEAKENED ON PURPOSE, disclosed. I intended to recompute the receipt digest and compare it to the stored sha256, but `canonicalDigest` is NOT on the @moe/runner public surface and task rail 2 forbids a deep import to reach it. Rather than reimplement canonical bytes in the test — which would be a second, drifting definition asserted against itself — the green case now proves provenance structurally: it feeds the stored receipt to the runner's own `receiptDigestInput`, which is the runner's ONE declaration of the bound field set, and asserts the returned field set contains recipeSha256, inputTreeSha256, resultTreeSha256, runtimeObservationSha256, timestamps, argv and the three identities, and that it does NOT contain sha256 (the digest provably does not cover itself). It also pins receiptVersion to the runner's EVIDENCE_RECEIPT_VERSION. The binding itself is proved by drill (2) and drill (5) in step 7, not by this assertion alone; I am flagging it so QA grades it as structural provenance, not as a digest recomputation.

`hermeticVerifierEnvironment` is used for the child environment rather than an assembled one — the service will pass it in step 5, so a caller cannot widen what a verifier sees.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT THE SERVICE. Create `foundation-verification-service.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge. Flow: resolve identities through the landed dispatch readers; verify the recipe seal with `recipeSealMatches`; commit ONE atomic verification activation; run `runVerifierProcess` with `createNodeProcessLauncher` and `hermeticVerifierEnvironment`; on an observed run build the receipt with `buildEvidenceReceipt` and persist it once; otherwise refuse with a stable code and layer and persist no receipt.
RETURN THE PRODUCERS' REFUSALS UNCHANGED. A `VerifierProcessRefusal` keeps its own `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES` member and `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS` layer; a store refusal keeps the store's. Do NOT restamp either into this service's vocabulary — that erases which layer answered, and four layers can answer here.
NEVER call `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`: they hand the callback a raw `DatabaseSync` and the no-new-schema rail forbids it. Use the narrow port the dispatch slice established, and verify it still cannot name them.
DO NOT MODIFY the producers — `packages/runner/src/evidence/**` belongs to task-69f2b6f7 and `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-*` to task-6cbff010, both DONE. This is the consumer edge; if a producer genuinely cannot be composed as written, report blocked rather than editing it.
Keep the file under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`. If it would exceed, split the persistence half into a sibling module with its own LF bridge rather than compressing — the dispatch slice was rejected partly for a 249-line service with no headroom, and the fix there was exactly this move.
Do NOT publish from apps/daemon/src/index.ts — index-surface.test.ts pins an exact export count and index.ts is not an owned path.

implementationPlan.description:
REPLAY AND THE READ MODEL — DoD 4 and DoD 5. Replay: re-run the same verification identity and assert the durable state holds EXACTLY ONE verification run and ONE receipt row, read back from the store rather than from the return value. Then the case that actually kills the echo defect: replay with a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT candidate and assert a distinct refusal with no overwritten history — the first receipt's bytes must still be there afterwards. On this board the store's replay identity has repeatedly failed to cover the events array, so a replay answered from the caller's own record makes every idempotence assertion compare the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes and pass forever.
READ MODEL: DoD 5 says prior receipts come back BYTE-IDENTICALLY. Implement the read to re-decode the durable bytes and byte-compare before returning — the same discipline `readStoredFoundationAttempt` uses, which re-encodes the decoded payload and refuses on drift. Assert byte identity against the originally persisted bytes, not against a re-derived object: two objects can be deep-equal while their canonical bytes differ, and it is the bytes review and closure will hash.
Assert the read model refuses rather than returning a partial answer when a stored receipt fails to decode or its digest does not recompute — an unreadable receipt is UNKNOWN, never an absent one, because "no receipt" and "unreadable receipt" lead a reviewer to opposite conclusions.
NAME THE CONSUMER: this read model exists for task-8f9305b9bb5e4b8db327a55981b2ea0e (Review-qualified goal closure), then the Foundation canary task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a. Record both ids.
implementationPlan.note:
REPLAY AND READ MODEL LANDED. Focused run EXIT=0, "Tests  20 passed (20)"; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT=0.

DoD 4 — REPLAY. Re-running the same identity leaves EXACTLY ONE RECEIPTED and ONE ACTIVATED event, counted from `store.readEvents` rather than from either return value, and the second call's digest equals the first's. The replay is answered from the DURABLE row before the wrapper is ever reached, so no second process starts — which also sidesteps `runVerifierProcess`'s module-level grant registry rather than depending on it. Replay with a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT candidate (a second sealed recipe with different argv, so a different sealed sha256) refuses FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_REPLAY_CONFLICT / DAEMON_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT, and the first receipt's BYTES are asserted byte-for-byte unchanged afterwards — history is not overwritten. The echo defect this step warns about is closed structurally: the replay comparison is between the caller's request and the DURABLE row's recipeSha256/recordDigest/attemptAggregateId, never between the caller's bytes and the caller's own bytes.

DoD 5 — READ MODEL. `readStoredReceipt` re-decodes the durable payload, RE-ENCODES it and byte-compares against what the store actually holds before returning, the same discipline `readStoredFoundationAttempt` uses. Four read-path cases, each pinning code and layer: byte-identical return (the returned row re-encodes to the ORIGINALLY PERSISTED bytes, not to a re-derived object, and its digest matches the write-path digest); AMBIGUOUS on a second receipt row; ABSENT on a verification that never ran; MALFORMED on an empty id.

ONE WEAKNESS I FOUND IN MY OWN TEST AND FIXED BEFORE MOVING ON. The byte-identity case as first written was nearly tautological: it decoded the stored bytes and re-encoded them, which a canonical codec makes true whether or not production compares anything — so drill (5) in step 7 would have found it green and I would have been strengthening it under time pressure. It is now backed by a case that only a real byte compare can pass: the same receipt object re-serialised NON-CANONICALLY with `JSON.stringify(value, null, 1)` and planted as a genuine RECEIPTED event through the store's own commit port. It decodes to a deep-equal row, so a read model that merely decoded would hand it back as authoritative evidence; production refuses FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT_UNREADABLE / DAEMON_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT. The case asserts the planted bytes really differ from the source bytes first, so it cannot pass vacuously.

That case also closed a coverage hole worth naming: before it, FOUNDATION_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT_UNREADABLE had a producer but NO test, which is exactly the orphan shape step 7 audits for — a code with an emit site nothing exercises is one refactor away from being unreachable and nobody would notice.

CONSUMERS RECORDED, as required: this read model exists for task-8f9305b9bb5e4b8db327a55981b2ea0e (Review-qualified goal closure) and then the Foundation canary task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a. Both hash the BYTES rather than compare objects, which is precisely why byte identity and not deep equality is what these cases assert; the reason is written into the describe block so the next reader does not weaken it back to a deep-equal check.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Restate the wrapper's execution codes in this service's vocabulary for a uniform error shape. REJECTED: `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES` and `VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS` already cover execution failures, and four layers can answer here — store, dispatch readers, wrapper, this service. Restamping erases which one did, and two vocabularies for one condition is precisely what got 6cbff010 rejected in round 2.

2) Accept the input/result manifests as payloads for convenience. REJECTED: DoD 1 forbids caller-supplied replacements, and the strongest form of that is structural — the input names identities only. A validated-away payload field is one refactor from being trusted.

3) Validate refusals wherever convenient and rely on the process failing later. REJECTED: a refusal after the process ran is a cleanup, not a refusal. Assert zero launcher invocations on every refusal path.

4) Run the wrapper first and commit the activation on success. REJECTED: that makes a run without a committed activation reachable — an effect nothing authorised. Activation first; a crash then leaves an activation with no run, which is the safe direction.

5) Treat a truncated capture as UNKNOWN and move on without recording the truncation. REJECTED: the truncation is itself the evidence that the capture is not a verdict. Recording it is what stops a later reader treating the retained output as complete.

6) Treat FAILED as UNKNOWN to be conservative. REJECTED — it looks safe and is not: it discards a real verdict the verifier produced, and downstream closure would then wait forever for evidence that already exists.

7) Assemble the verifier environment locally. REJECTED: `hermeticVerifierEnvironment` is published so a caller cannot widen what a verifier sees; a local env is a second, drifting definition of hermetic.

8) Return the read model's decoded object without byte-comparing. REJECTED: two objects can be deep-equal while their canonical bytes differ, and it is the bytes review and closure will hash. Re-decode and byte-compare, as `readStoredFoundationAttempt` already does.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD f65fbde. This task has TWO hard dependencies and the cascade cleared only one — I checked both: `task-69f2b6f7` (Verification process wrapper) DONE, `task-6cbff010` (Durable Claude attempt dispatch) DONE. `apps/daemon/src/evidence/` does not exist; this task creates it.

I PLANNED 6cbff010'S ROUND-2 FIX EARLIER THIS SESSION, and it landed as designed: the compose+commit moved into the store, which is now 235 lines with `settleFoundationAttempt` (:165) and `recordProvenFoundationAttempt` (:203), while the service came down from 249 to 213. LINE NUMBERS MOVED in that refactor, so every citation here is re-measured rather than carried over.

THE DISPATCH READ SURFACE this task consumes (apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-store.ts): `readDurableFoundationObservation` (:77), `commitFoundationPhase` (:103), `readFoundationReservationDigest` (:119), `readStoredFoundationAttempt` (:132), `readFoundationAttemptRecord` (:153), `settleFoundationAttempt` (:165), `FoundationAttemptCapture` (:181), `recordProvenFoundationAttempt` (:203). Service exports `createFoundationAttemptService` (:97).

THE WRAPPER SURFACE IS FULLY PUBLISHED FROM THE RUNNER ROOT via surface/evidence-surface.ts, so task rail 2's no-deep-imports constraint costs nothing: `buildVerificationRecipe`/`recipeSealMatches`; `runVerifierProcess`/`createNodeProcessLauncher` with `RunVerifierProcessInput/Ok/Refused/Result`, `VerifierLaunchSpec`, `VerifierExitObservation`; `buildEvidenceReceipt`/`receiptDigestInput` with `EvidenceReceipt`, `EvidenceReceiptBody`, `ReceiptTimestamps`; `canonicalObligations`/`ObligationContext`; `EXECUTION_DISPOSITIONS`/`observedExecutionRejection`/`ObservedVerifierExecution`/`ObservedOutput`; `VERIFIER_PROCESS_ERROR_CODES`/`VERIFIER_PROCESS_LAYERS`/`MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES`/`MAX_VERIFIER_RUN_MS`/`VERIFIER_REAP_GRACE_MS`/`hermeticVerifierEnvironment`/`VerifierActivation`/`VerifierCapture`/`VerifierClock`; `VerificationRecipe`/`VerificationRecipeBody`/`VerifierIdentity`.

THE HARD DISTINCTION, and the reason this task is CRITICAL rather than mechanical: a PROVEN FAILED verification is authoritative evidence — the recipe ran, the verifier answered, the answer was no. An UNVERIFIED run is evidence of nothing. Collapsing them in either direction is a defect: treating UNKNOWN as failure INVENTS a verdict; treating FAILED as UNKNOWN DISCARDS one. `EXECUTION_DISPOSITIONS` and `observedExecutionRejection` are the vocabulary that keeps them apart, and DoD 3 is entirely about not letting them merge.

THE FALSE-PASS PATH is truncation. `MAX_VERIFIER_OUTPUT_BYTES` bounds the capture, and a truncated capture whose retained output happens to look green is exactly how an authoritative passing receipt gets minted from an unverified run. The truncation must be RECORDED, not silently dropped.

ENFORCE DoD 1 BY TYPE, NOT BY VALIDATION. "Caller-supplied replacements refuse" is strongest when the replacement is structurally unrepresentable in the input type — the input names IDENTITIES, never payloads. A validated-away field is one refactor from being trusted.

ORDERING IS OBSERVABLE AND MUST BE ASSERTED AS SUCH: refusals before wrapper invocation (assert ZERO recorded launcher invocations, the shape 6cbff010's `forgedCalls 0` assertion used), and activation committed before the run (a run without a committed activation is an effect nothing authorised).

REPLAY: this board has repeatedly found that the store's replay identity does not cover the events array, so only a CHANGED-CANDIDATE replay detects an implementation that echoes the caller.
planningNotes.risks:
1) COLLAPSING FAILED AND UNKNOWN, in either direction. Treating UNKNOWN as failure invents a verdict; treating FAILED as UNKNOWN discards one and stalls closure. Drill 3 covers both directions.

2) TRUNCATION MINTING A FALSE PASS. A bounded capture whose retained bytes look green is the concrete route to an authoritative passing receipt from an unverified run. Drill 2 is the most important drill in the plan.

3) A REFUSAL AFTER THE PROCESS RAN is not a refusal. Assert zero launcher invocations on every refusal path — 6cbff010 proved this assertion shape works.

4) A RUN WITHOUT A COMMITTED ACTIVATION is an effect nothing authorised. Order matters and must be asserted from durable state, not from control flow.

5) THE REPLAY-ECHO DEFECT has recurred repeatedly on this board because the store's replay identity does not cover the events array. Only a changed-candidate replay detects it; a same-candidate replay compares the caller's bytes with the caller's bytes.

6) FOUR LAYERS CAN REFUSE. Pin code AND layer everywhere, and build each fixture valid at the earlier layers or a different layer answers and the assertion quietly stops testing its subject.

7) AN ORPHAN CODE CANNOT FAIL CLOSED. 6cbff010 was rejected in round 2 for three declared-but-unproduced codes. Grep every member of the new vocabulary for a producer before the gate, and drop what has none.

8) LINE BUDGET. 6cbff010's service sat at 249 of 250 with no headroom and the fix was to move persistence into a sibling. Plan for that split from the start rather than compressing.

9) A HELD SQLITE HANDLE kills the vitest worker; real store per test, closed in a `finally` on every exit path including throws. A timed-out verifier case must itself be bounded, or a hang reports no verdict at all.

10) DAEMON GATES RED AT BASELINE from foreign in-flight slices. Record the before-set; only the owned-path delta must be empty. Read the count line — exit 0 with no count line ran nothing.

11) CONSUMERS: task-8f9305b9bb5e4b8db327a55981b2ea0e (Review-qualified goal closure), then canary task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a. Record both rather than assuming the edge.
